jobs.title: Director, AI Product Ops
jobs.description:
Director, AI Product Ops — Direct Tax & Audit Product

Job Description

We are seeking an exceptional, transformative Director of AI Product Ops
to lead the operational and cultural evolution of Thomson Reuters' Direct Tax & Audit product
organization.

In this exciting opportunity as Director, AI Product Ops
, you will evolve our traditional program and operations function into a lean, AI-first Product Ops office. Your mission is two-fold: drive operational excellence across our entire software portfolio with "near-zero-overhead," and spearhead our AI maturity program, moving our teams from basic personal productivity to advanced, agent-driven workflows.

This is a hands-on, builder's seat designed to modernize how our teams work. You will serve as a critical catalyst for product innovation and foster faster, more effective ways of working across the team. By automating coordination and program management tasks, you will not only liberate our product teams from administrative overhead, but enable them to focus on deep customer discovery, modern product craft, and high-velocity execution—ultimately delivering superior customer experiences, higher-quality products, and stronger commercial value for Thomson Reuters. You will lead a small, senior team of product ops experts and carry a Direct Tax & Audit-wide change-management mandate.

Scope of the Estate

Your operational mandate spans the entire Direct Tax & Audit product landscape:

The Core Portfolio ("Bedrock"): Our market-leading, established suite of tax and accounting products.
The Agentic Stack ("Catalyst"): Our cutting-edge, agent-first platform powering experiences like CoCounsel and Ready to Review.

Key Responsibilities

AI-First Product Operations
Drive a Near-Zero-Overhead Model: Architect and run product operations where AI agents automate traditional coordination tasks—such as status reporting, dependency tracking, and cross-functional communications—allowing humans to focus on product judgment and execution.
Streamline the Product Estate: Own product operations across both the Core ("Bedrock") and Agentic ("Catalyst") portfolios, unifying them under a single, highly efficient, and modern operating rhythm.
Bridge Multi-Product Dependencies: Own the dependency seam where product commitments break. Build automated tooling and visibility systems to expose cross-team dependencies, GTM milestones, and timelines across Catalyst and Bedrock applications.
Support Modern SDLC Workflows: Ensure that all operational processes and visibility tools integrate seamlessly with our suite of modern agile and AI tools (e.g., Linear, Slack, GitHub, Claude) so that the operational backbone supports, rather than slows down, rapid engineering sprint cycles.
Partner on Migrations: Collaborate with Customer Success to integrate large-scale customer migrations smoothly into the product-ops framework without interrupting core product execution.
Define & Execute against Metrics that Matter: Move the organization away from vanity metrics toward metrics that drive the business forward. Execute a regular cadence that moves the metrics and the business.
AI Transformation across Direct Tax & Audit
Drive the AI-Maturity Roadmap: Lead Direct Tax & Audit's evolution from Level 1 AI usage (individual productivity tools) to Level 2 (shared team infrastructure: e.g., shared prompts, MCP integrations, shared skills) and toward Level 3 (agents acting on systems of record) and beyond.
Enable Modern PM Ways of Working: Use the AI-maturity transformation as the vehicle to elevate the PM craft. Lead enablement of PMs on using modern AI tools (e.g., Cursor, v0, Claude Code) and AI-first product development.
Build Shared Capability Playbooks: Establish and scale the internal playbooks (covering shared context, agentic workflows, model evaluations, and prompt libraries) that teams adopt as standard, reusable infrastructure.
Leadership, Change Management & Team Evolution
Build and Lead a High Impact Team: Recruit, mentor, and manage a high-performing, lean team of senior program-ops experts, establishing a strong operational cadence and a high bar for talent & execution.
Execute a Direct Tax & Audit -wide Mandate: Act as an influential change agent across Direct Tax & Audit, brokering alignment and operational commitments with product, engineering, and design teams outside your direct reporting line.
Drive the Transformation Drumbeat & Communications: In close partnership with the Head of Direct Tax & Audit Product and the Direct Tax & Audit Product Leadership Team, design and lead a comprehensive change-management communications strategy. Establish a regular, engaging organizational 'drumbeat' to share wins, spotlight successful AI-enabled behaviors, reinforce new ways of working, and maintain high transformation momentum across the division.

You’re a fit for this role, if your background includes:

AI-Native: You have successfully driven a real organization or department up the AI maturity curve (L1 to L2/L3). You think in terms of systemic capability and shipped outcomes, and you are highly fluent in modern AI tooling (agents, prompt engineering, MCP, evals, and prototyping).
Modern Product-Ops & SDLC Advocate: You value lean, automated systems and shared team infrastructure over traditional, heavy PMO ceremony. You understand modern software development lifecycles (SDLC) and how to design operational systems that help modern PMs, Engineers, and Designers build software faster.
Ambidextrous Operator: Equally credible and comfortable operating across complex, high-transaction legacy architectures (Bedrock) and fast-moving, agent-first modern stacks (Catalyst).
Transformational Change Leader: You are an inspiring evangelist who drives cultural and behavioral shifts by building excitement, capturing buy-in, and bringing teams along on the journey. Rather than relying on top-down mandates, you lead with influence, empathy, and positive reinforcement to align cross-functional partners around a shared vision.
Hands-on AI Fluency: You are a daily, active user of agentsand LLMs. You possess intuitive, practical knowledge of how generative AI tools can optimize a product team's day-to-day work.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in program management, product operations, or technical operations leadership at scale.
Deep familiarity with modern product management practices (ideally within modern tech, high-growth startups, or progressive B2B SaaS), with a clear understanding of how modern PM, Engineering, and Design squads collaborate.
Proven experience implementing modern agile SDLC structures and automating project-tracking workflows.
Experience in regulated or professional software industries (e.g., tax, legal, audit, finance, or compliance) where data security, accuracy, and AI governance are critical is a strong plus.
Demonstrated track record of leading change-management and communication initiatives, upskilling teams, and inspiring cultural transformations to adopt modern, technical capabilities.
Demonstrated track record of leading change management initiatives, upskilling teams, and transitioning legacy roles into modern, technical capabilities.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Business, Engineering, Management Information Systems, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Business, Engineering, Management Information Systems, or a related field.

This posting is for proactive recruitment purposes and may be used to fill current openings or future vacancies within our organization.

What’s in it For You?

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

Our use of AI within the recruitment process Thomson Reuters utilizes Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support parts of our global recruitment process. Unless you opt-out, our AI system will assess the information provided by you and compare it to the requirements listed for the role, and present the result to our recruitment personnel for further review. The AI system acts as a supporting tool, but there is always a human making the decision if you will be considered for the role.

In the United States, Thomson Reuters offers a comprehensive benefits package to our employees. Our benefit package includes market competitive health, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance programs, as well as a competitive 401k plan with company match. In addition, Thomson Reuters offers market leading work life benefits with competitive vacation, sick and safe paid time off, paid holidays (including two company mental health days off), parental leave, sabbatical leave. These benefits meet or exceeds the requirements of paid time off in accordance with any applicable state or municipal laws. Finally, Thomson Reuters offers the following additional benefits: optional hospital, accident and sickness insurance paid 100% by the employee; optional life and AD&D insurance paid 100% by the employee; Flexible Spending and Health Savings Accounts; fitness reimbursement; access to Employee Assistance Program; Group Legal Identity Theft Protection benefit paid 100% by employee; access to 529 Plan; commuter benefits; Adoption & Surrogacy Assistance; Tuition Reimbursement; and access to Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

Thomson Reuters complies with local laws that require upfront disclosure of the expected pay range for a position. The base compensation range varies across locations. Eligible office location(s) for this role include one or more of the following: New York City, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and/or Irvine, CA; McLean, VA; Washington, DC. The base compensation range for the role in any of those locations is $181,400 USD - $337,000 USD. jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

As the Senior Director, Strategy Risk Business Operations and Shared Services you will lead a high-performing team of directors, senior managers, and managers to drive strategic, operational, and financial excellence within RBC’s Commercial & Payment Technology (CPT) portfolio. This critical leadership role is accountable for Financial Management, Project Portfolio Planning, Vendor Management, Risk & Compliance, and Strategic Planning, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities and delivering exceptional business outcomes. You will champion employee engagement, change management, and innovation (e.g., AI adoption) while maintaining rigorous governance and operational excellence.

What You'll Do

Leadership & Strategy

Lead the Planning, Risk & Governance functions, overseeing financial management, project portfolio planning, and strategic alignment with RBC’s Commercial Banking and T&O objectives.
Develop and execute CPT’s 5-year strategic plan, leveraging internal/external research and partnering with business executives to drive disciplined project management.
Champion enterprise initiatives (e.g., AI/AIDLC) and change management within CPT, ensuring successful adoption and engagement.
Foster exceptional employee engagement through targeted strategies and communication plans in partnership with Enterprise Communications.

Risk & Governance

Ensure adherence to Risk & Governance policies, standards, and control points (e.g., audits, access reviews, compliance attestations).
Lead T&O and RBC-initiated Risk & Governance campaigns, collaborating with Risk, GS, and business partners.
Oversee Business Continuity Management (BCM), including plan approvals, testing, and strategy.
Monitor Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and escalate issues, ensuring alignment with first-line defense (Internal/External Audit).

Vendor Management

Lead the expansion of Vendor Management, optimizing on-shore/off-shore resources and negotiating multi-million-dollar contracts.
Drive cost savings, efficiencies, and service standards across vendor relationships, ensuring alignment with financial and operational targets.

Financial Management & Reporting

Define and execute the Financial Plan for application maintenance, development, and Risk & Governance efforts.
Provide timely, actionable financial reporting (budgets, forecasts, metrics) to the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) and stakeholders.
Manage IT Development, Maintenance, and Financial budgets, ensuring alignment with annual and 5-year plans.
Oversee project accruals, cost accounting, and vendor invoice management to meet overhead and recovery targets.

Operational Excellence & Performance

Monitor performance metrics, scorecards, and dashboards, driving process improvements and benchmarking.
Lead Program/Project onboarding/closure, ensuring accurate financial tracking in systems (e.g., Planview, MIS).
Leverage AI and automation for reporting and project delivery efficiencies.

People Leadership

Build and mentor a high-performing team, aligning individual goals with RBC’s Leadership Model.
Drive diversity, reward & recognition, and career development initiatives.
Instill a culture of change readiness and empowerment across CPT.

What You Need To Succeed

Must Have:

15+ years of leadership experience in Technology, Financial Services, or Operations, with expertise in Risk, Governance, and Vendor Management.
Proven track record in strategic planning, financial management, and large-scale project delivery.
Strong understanding of AI, Agile/SDLC methodologies, and regulatory compliance.
Exceptional negotiation, stakeholder management, and communication skills.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or related field; MBA or advanced certification preferred.

Nice to Have:

Payments industry experience

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
Opportunities to do challenging work
Opportunities to take on progressively greater accountabilities
Opportunities to building close relationships with clients

jobs.title: Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation | Director of Software Technology and Innovation
jobs.description:
Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

À propos de Crowe BGK

Depuis 75 ans, Crowe BGK S.E.N.C.R.L. est un chef de file de confiance en matière de services de comptabilité et de conseil au Canada. Notre équipe compte plus de 250 professionnels qui servent nos clients à partir de nos bureaux de Montréal et d’Ottawa. Nous offrons des services d’audit, de fiscalité, de conseil et de consultation, aidant les particuliers et les sociétés privées à relever des défis complexes. Nous sommes fiers d’avoir été nommés parmi les 100 meilleurs employeurs de PME au Canada et parmi les meilleurs employeurs de Montréal, car nous croyons qu’il est essentiel de créer un milieu de travail où les gens se sentent soutenus, valorisés et inspirés à progresser.

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

expérimenté(e) et pratique pour aider Crowe BGK à maintenir un environnement technologique fiable et à faire progresser l’utilisation des logiciels à l’échelle du cabinet. La personne retenue combinera une compréhension des processus d’affaires, une discipline opérationnelle et une expertise technologique afin d’améliorer le service à la clientèle, l’efficacité, l’évolutivité et l’expérience employé.

Vous Serez Responsable De

Stratégie et gouvernance des logiciels d’entreprise

Élaborer et maintenir la feuille de route pluriannuelle des applications du cabinet, l’inventaire des logiciels, le modèle de propriété et la gouvernance pour la sélection, les accès, les changements, les intégrations, les renouvellements et le retrait.
Identifier les lacunes en matière de capacités, les dédoublements, les outils sous-utilisés ou non pris en charge ainsi que les occasions émergentes; conseiller le ou la COFO, les associé(e)s et la direction sur les priorités, les investissements, les compromis, la normalisation et les coûts.

Amélioration des processus d’affaires et innovation

Analyser et repenser les processus dans les services à la clientèle et les fonctions corporatives, en mobilisant les parties prenantes afin de résoudre les irritants, les lacunes de contrôle, le travail à refaire, les problèmes de données et les besoins non satisfaits avant l’automatisation.
Utiliser les données et les commentaires pour prioriser les améliorations à forte valeur ajoutée et évaluer les flux de travail, l’automatisation, l’analytique, l’intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes en tenant compte de la confidentialité, de la qualité, des contrôles et de la supervision humaine appropriés.

Évaluation des logiciels et analyses de rentabilité

Traduire les besoins d’affaires en exigences mesurables sur les plans fonctionnel, technique, des données, de la sécurité, de l’intégration, des contrôles, du service et des utilisateurs; diriger les démonstrations, les projets pilotes, les vérifications de références, les grilles d’évaluation, la diligence raisonnable des fournisseurs et la comparaison objective des risques et des solutions de rechange.
Préparer et présenter des analyses de rentabilité pour les décisions d’aller de l’avant ou non, couvrant le coût total de possession, le rendement du capital investi, les échéanciers, les ressources, l’incidence du changement, la formation, l’atténuation des risques, le soutien et les coûts de sortie; soutenir les négociations commerciales et contractuelles.

Gouvernance et responsabilité de la mise en œuvre

Agir à titre de responsable imputable du volet affaires et technologie, en partenariat avec le ou la gestionnaire de projet attitré(e), afin de définir la portée, les résultats, le budget, les ressources, la gouvernance, les jalons, les droits décisionnels, les risques, les communications et les mesures de succès.
Coordonner les parties prenantes et veiller à la conception des processus, à la configuration, aux intégrations, à la conversion des données, aux essais, aux contrôles, à la formation, à la mise en production, au soutien, à la préparation, à la stabilisation, à l’adoption et à la réalisation des bénéfices; faire remonter les lacunes importantes et maintenir la visibilité auprès de la direction.

Gestion du portefeuille, des fournisseurs, des données et des risques

Gérer les budgets logiciels, les licences, l’utilisation, les renouvellements, les fournisseurs, les contrats, les niveaux de service, les indicateurs du portefeuille, la rationalisation et le retrait des solutions.
Collaborer avec les ressources en TI, cybersécurité, protection de la vie privée, affaires juridiques et gestion des risques afin d’encadrer les intégrations, les données, les contrôles d’accès, la continuité des activités, les risques liés aux tiers, l’intelligence artificielle et l’automatisation.

Leadership du changement et mobilisation des parties prenantes

Établir des relations de confiance avec les associé(e)s, les dirigeant(e)s, le personnel, les fournisseurs et les prestataires de services; diriger les employé(e)s attitré(e)s et les équipes interfonctionnelles en assurant une responsabilisation claire et une forte orientation vers le service.
Diriger les communications, la formation, l’adoption, la documentation, le soutien et la propriété des applications; développer des ambassadeurs internes, contribuer au plan d’affaires du cabinet et tenir le ou la COFO ainsi que les parties prenantes informés.

Autorité et responsabilité

Responsable du portefeuille de logiciels, de la feuille de route des applications, des normes de gouvernance et de la direction des équipes de mise en œuvre des TI et des processus dans le cadre de la stratégie et des budgets approuvés; peut exiger les examens appropriés en matière d’affaires, de sécurité, de protection de la vie privée, d’intégration, de contrôle et de mise en œuvre.
Recommande la sélection, le séquencement, le renouvellement, l’expansion, la consolidation ou le retrait des logiciels; peut suspendre ou faire remonter les préoccupations non résolues et est responsable de la qualité des recommandations, de la gouvernance de la mise en œuvre, de l’adoption, de la stabilisation et des bénéfices approuvés.

Mesures de succès

Gérer un inventaire à jour des logiciels, une propriété claire, une gouvernance rigoureuse, une feuille de route approuvée, des analyses de rentabilité crédibles et des dépenses contrôlées.
Réaliser les mises en œuvre avec une gouvernance, une préparation, des contrôles, une adoption et un soutien durable efficaces, ainsi qu’avec la réalisation des bénéfices approuvés.
Obtenir des améliorations mesurables en matière d’efficacité, de capacité, de qualité, de fiabilité des données, d’expérience employé et client, de performance des fournisseurs, de gestion des risques et de confiance des parties prenantes.

Les Qualifications Qui Comptent

Baccalauréat en systèmes d’information, administration des affaires, comptabilité, finance, informatique, génie ou dans un domaine connexe; une combinaison équivalente de formation et d’expérience sera considérée.
Sept années ou plus d’expérience progressive en logiciels, systèmes d’affaires, amélioration des processus, transformation technologique, gestion de produits ou gestion de programmes, dont au moins trois années dans un rôle de leadership ou de responsabilité à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
Une expérience dans un cabinet comptable ou un autre environnement de services professionnels est privilégiée, avec une compréhension des décisions dirigées par les associé(e)s, du service à la clientèle soumis à des échéanciers, de la confidentialité et du changement entre les groupes de pratique.
Succès démontré dans la direction d’évaluations de logiciels, d’analyses de rentabilité, de sélection de fournisseurs et de mise en œuvre de solutions SaaS à l’échelle du cabinet ou de l’entreprise.
Expérience pratique de la cartographie et de la refonte des processus, des exigences, des essais, de la formation, de la gestion du changement et de la réalisation des bénéfices.

Vous Pouvez Compter Sur Nous Pour

Une rémunération compétitive
Un modèle de travail hybride flexible
Des assurances collectives complètes dès le premier jour d’emploi pour soutenir votre bien-être global
Des vacances généreuses et 8 journées personnelles pour responsabilités familiales
Des fermetures du cabinet pendant les Fêtes pour décrocher pleinement
Des vendredis d’été avec fermeture hâtive durant la saison estivale
Stationnement gratuit sur place ou remboursement du transport en commun
Une allocation annuelle mieux-être pour soutenir la santé physique et mentale
Une allocation pour l’aménagement du bureau à domicile afin d’assurer un environnement confortable et productif
Une culture de bureau dynamique et accueillante, où les chiens sont les bienvenus et où l’énergie est au rendez-vous. Entre les 5 à 7 animés, les cours de spinning hebdomadaires, les ateliers de peinture en équipe, les soirées quiz et karaoké, il y a toujours une activité rassembleuse. Sans oublier notre Camp Crowe, une expérience estivale unique remplie d’activités amusantes qui favorisent la camaraderie et créent des souvenirs mémorables

Si vous cherchez un endroit où vos idées comptent et où votre carrière peut s'épanouir, postulez dès aujourd'hui!

Cultivez votre curiosité. Inspirez votre esprit. Façonnez votre carrière.

Nous maintenons un environnement de travail inclusif et offrant des chances égales afin que chaque professionnel de Crowe BGK puisse réaliser son potentiel d'évolution. Nous considérons tous les candidats qualifiés pour un emploi sans distinction de race, de couleur, de religion, de sexe, d'orientation sexuelle, d'identité de genre, d'origine nationale, d'âge, d'état matrimonial, de handicap, de statut d'ancien combattant protégé ou de tout autre facteur protégé par la loi.

Nous remercions tous les candidats pour leur intérêt et nous ne contacterons que ceux que nous souhaitons poursuivre.

Director of Software Technology and Innovation

About Crowe BGK

For 75 years, Crowe BGK LLP has been a trusted leader in accounting and advisory services in Canada. We are a team of 250+ professionals serving clients from our Montreal and Ottawa offices. We provide audit, tax, advisory, and consulting services, helping individuals and private companies navigate complex challenges. We’re proud to be named one of Canada’s Top 100 SME Employers and one of Montreal’s Top Employers, because we believe in creating a workplace where people feel supported, valued, and inspired to grow.

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Director of Software Technology and Innovation

to help Crowe BGK maintain a reliable technology environment and advance the use of software across the firm. The successful candidate will combine business process insight, operational discipline, and technology expertise to improve client service, efficiency, scalability, and the employee experience.

You Will Be Accountable For

Enterprise Software Strategy and Governance

Develop and maintain the firm's multi-year application roadmap, software inventory, ownership model, and governance for selection, access, changes, integrations, renewals, and retirement.
Identify capability gaps, duplication, underused or unsupported tools, and emerging opportunities; advise the COFO, partners, and leadership on priorities, investments, trade-offs, standardization, and cost.

Business Process Improvement and Innovation

Analyze and redesign processes across client service and corporate functions, engaging stakeholders to address pain points, control gaps, rework, data issues, and unmet needs before automation.
Use data and feedback to prioritize high-value improvements and evaluate workflow, automation, analytics, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies with appropriate confidentiality, quality, controls, and human oversight.

Software Evaluation and Business Cases

Translate business needs into measurable functional, technical, data, security, integration, control, service, and use

The work you'll do is more than just a job.

At the State of Minnesota, employees play a critical role in developing policies, providing essential services, and working to improve the well-being and quality of life for all Minnesotans. The State of Minnesota is committed to equity and inclusion, and invests in employees by providing benefits, support resources, and training and development opportunities.

Minnesota Management and Budget (MMB) is seeking a Chief Data Officer (CDO) to serve as the State of Minnesota’s enterprise leader for statewide data strategy, governance, and ethical use. This position will set the vision for how data can strengthen program integrity and overall government performance. As the lead of the Minnesota Data Strategy Team, the CDO will build the legal, technical, and operational foundation that allows agencies to securely and responsibly use and share data, while guiding commissioners, executives, and cross-sector partners through complex policy and privacy considerations.

This role pairs strategic leadership with practical problem-solving, setting a statewide vision for data infrastructure by building collaboration across a federated data environment. The CDO will be a trusted advisor on law, ethics, and information policy, driving long-term improvements of the state’s data ecosystem and helping ensure Minnesotans benefit from well-governed, high-quality data.

Job Duties For This Position Include

Providing executive leadership for the Minnesota Data Strategy Team (MDST), directing managers, staff, and cross-agency partners to implement statewide data governance and privacy priorities
Establishing strategic, operational, and legal direction for the MDST, incorporating input from commissioners and executive leaders while making final determinations on statewide priorities
Advising senior leaders on the strategic, legal, and ethical considerations of data sharing and use, and directing implementation of governance mechanisms that balance innovation, privacy, risk mitigation, and accountability
Serving as the statewide point of escalation for complex, novel, or cross-agency legal issues affecting enterprise data sharing and governance

jobs.title: Director, AI Engineering - Manufacturing
jobs.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

Role Summary

We are seeking a senior engineering and AI/ML leader to build and lead a distributed team of AI/ML engineers supporting manufacturing sites across the company. Based in Bangkok or the UK or Canada and reporting to the Chief AI Officer, this role will translate high-value manufacturing problems into reliable, scalable AI systems that improve productivity, quality, yield, equipment performance, and operational decision-making.

The ideal candidate brings 15+ years of experience across engineering management, software engineering, AI/ML systems, and data science, combined with deep practical knowledge of manufacturing environments. This leader must be equally comfortable setting technical direction, coaching engineers, partnering with plant and business leaders, and working close to the factory floor to move solutions from discovery through production adoption.

Leadership Scope

Lead, grow, and develop a distributed team of AI/ML engineers who work across manufacturing sites and solve site-specific operational problems.
Establish the technical vision, engineering standards, delivery practices, and talent strategy for manufacturing AI across the organization.
Create a strong partnership model with plant leadership, manufacturing engineering, process engineering, yield, quality, operations, IT, and enterprise data teams.
Balance local site responsiveness with reusable platforms, common architectures, shared components, and responsible AI practices that scale across plants.

Key Responsibilities

Set and execute a multi-year roadmap for AI/ML applications in manufacturing, aligned to business priorities and measurable operational outcomes.
Identify and prioritize high-impact opportunities across process optimization, yield improvement, visual inspection, defect classification, predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, root-cause analysis, quality, scheduling, and engineering productivity.
Guide the architecture, design, development, validation, deployment, and lifecycle management of production-grade AI/ML systems used in manufacturing workflows.
Define engineering patterns for data pipelines, feature and model management, experiment tracking, APIs, user interfaces, monitoring, cybersecurity, reliability, and model performance management.
Ensure solutions work with real manufacturing data and systems, including MES, SPC, QMS, equipment and sensor data, inspection systems, yield systems, ERP, databases, engineering reports, and other structured and unstructured sources.
Drive disciplined problem definition and value measurement, connecting technical delivery to improvements in cycle time, throughput, yield, scrap, quality, cost, safety, and decision speed.
Partner with site teams to understand workflows, constraints, process variation, data quality, user needs, and adoption barriers; ensure solutions are usable by engineers, operators, and business stakeholders.
Build and maintain strong relationships with senior manufacturing and technology leaders, communicating technical tradeoffs, risks, investment needs, and results with clarity.
Promote effective use of classical machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, optimization, statistical methods, LLMs, and generative AI where they are fit for purpose.
Establish governance for responsible, secure, explainable, and maintainable AI in manufacturing, including validation, human oversight, change control, and production support.

Required Qualifications

15+ years of progressive experience in software engineering, AI/ML engineering, data science, or a closely related technical discipline, including significant leadership experience.
Bachelor's or master's degree in engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, industrial engineering, data science, or a related field; advanced technical education is preferred.
Deep hands-on understanding of software engineering practices, distributed systems, cloud or edge architectures, APIs, data platforms, testing, observability, security, and production operations.
Practical knowledge of manufacturing processes, process variation, yield, quality systems, equipment data, inspection, traceability, root-cause analysis, and the realities of plant operations.
Willingness and ability to travel 30% or more to manufacturing sites and partner locations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in semiconductor, photonics, electronics, optical components, precision manufacturing, or other high-volume advanced manufacturing environments.
Experience with manufacturing software and data ecosystems such as MES, SPC, QMS, ERP, equipment automation, inspection platforms, historian systems, and yield management systems.
Experience scaling AI/ML capabilities across multiple plants, regions, or business units with different processes, data maturity, and operating models.
Experience applying generative AI, knowledge retrieval, agentic workflows, or LLM-enabled tools to manufacturing, engineering, quality, or operations use cases.
